summary: S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras (~1877–1881). He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1884–1890) as an assistant to Robert Sewell.

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University (1977–1991) under Etienne Vermeersch. He was a director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
S. N. Krishna is an Indology researcher who was a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva (attested 2026).
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri worked in philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras, where he was attested as Reader in Indian Philosophy in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1942.

S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian. He served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1985–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Srikanta Sastri worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1922–1926) under M. H. Krishna, held a post at the University of Mysore (~1928–1966), and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

Saba Mahmood was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. She studied at the University of Washington and completed her PhD at Stanford (~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and UC Berkeley (2004–2018), where she taught Thomas Borchert.
Sabine Klein-Schwind works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and was attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

Sabine Löhr is an Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing an M.A. and doctoral studies under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a student/research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1991–1997) and founded the organization Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929), taught Alan Watts, and held teaching posts at the American Academy of Asian Studies and the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Sachin Kathale works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.
Sachindra Kumar Maity is an Indologist and historian. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1953–1957) and held a post at Jadavpur University (~1958).

Sadajiro Sugiura was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D.), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, succeeding Sakunoshin Motoda in 1923.
Saerji works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, serving on the faculty at Peking University, where he was an associate professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sai Susarla works in computational Indology. He served as Dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Said Reza Huseini is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2011–2016), and Leiden University (~2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi was a historian of religion who studied under Mohammad Habib and at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held posts at Aligarh Muslim University, Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).

Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Peter Harvey and Max Deeg, earning an M.Phil. from Cardiff University by 2014. He was attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.
